Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: What are the most common mistakes that startups make?
Answer: Ford River Rouge Complex was built during the 1920’s, and took over a decade to be completed. The manufacturing facility had 93 buildings with a total of nearly 16 million square feet (1.5 km2) of covered area. Ford’s plant had nearly 100 miles (160 km) of interior railroad track, had its own power plant and sat in a land area of 1.5 miles (2.4 km) wide by 1 mile (1.6 km) long. For years, Henry Ford employed over 100,000 workers at this location — even during the Great Depression of the 1930s. Can you imagine the initial capital investment to build such a massive car assembly plant? During the Industrial Age, starting a business demanded huge INITIAL investments — yet most of these businesses had insignificant customer acquisition costs (CAC). So to answer your question, by far… the #1 mistake I see startup entrepreneurs make in today’s economy is ignoring this. Listen, save your money, don’t even start a business until you fully understand this: Today, we live in a world of abundance, and this changes everything! While it’s true that today it’s cheaper than ever to start a business — it’s also now more expensive than ever for businesses to acquire new customers! Today most entrepreneurs fail NOT because they had a bad idea, but because they completely ignore this simple fact: CLV > (CAC + COGS) = Profits! Listen, if a business is unable find a cheap way to acquire customers they will sooner or later “choke” themselves to death burning money forever. It’s now critical for entrepreneurs not only to consider the initial investment required to get their business up and running — but most importantly they MUST budget enough capital to be able to acquire enough customers until they can break-even. Business has changed. Entrepreneurship has changed. #BeBusinessSmart

Question: How should I earn a lot of money from Quora? Is it true?
Answer: Yes, it’s true! You can make a lot of money from Quora, but you need to be like Bill Gates. Most want to meet Warren Buffett, hoping to get money from him, thinking, “Mr. Buffett has too much money. If I become his friend, I will make money from him.” Bill Gates has a different approach, thinking, “Mr. Buffett has too much knowledge, if I become his friend, I’m sure he will mentor me.” To answer your question, can you make a lot of money from Quora? Yes, if you approach this platform with the intention to make a few dollars, you may eventually, true! But if you want to make a lot of money from Quora, you need to take the knowledge found in the platform to do so. Quora is not a charity. Quora doesn’t “give” you money. Quora makes money from us, the users. This lesson applies to everything in life. Don’t approach businesses or people thinking, “What can I take from them.” With this mindset you will ALWAYS lose. But … Be like Bill Gates and Warren Buffett, who have both nurtured their friendship, not for the money they can take from each other. Imagine the money they have both made, nevertheless, resulting from each other’s knowledge. Quora has enough free knowledge available for you to learn how to make lots of money. I can assure you that if you read my over one thousand answers in this platform, you will. Never forget this: in today’s world, money is the result of knowledge. #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: What is the #1 thing necessary for being successful in life?
Answer: Luigi wants to be like Mario. Luigi strives to work like Mario, and dreams to achieve what Mario has achieved. Luigi hustles daily to own the car that Mario drives. Luigi dreams to own a big house like Mario’s house. Luigi wants what Mario wants. Luigi is also influenced by the irrational lifestyle of Instagram influencers he follows. Luigi is continuously polluting his brain with JUNK. As time goes by, Luigi’s habits are gradually stealing his freedom to think for himself and pursue his OWN passions and dreams. Eventually Luigi loses his sense of identity and ultimately becomes chronically unsatisfied. Now, to answer the question, what is the #1 thing necessary for being successful in life? YOUR FREEDOM! Stop measuring success by monetary measures. Success should not be exclusively measured by your ability to accumulate material possessions. Don’t ever compare yourself to others; this impulse is the result of us going through the archaic educational system and the standardized tests that were continuously evaluating and comparing us to each other. Success should be measured by YOUR personal satisfaction, by enjoying the freedom to live YOUR life to the fullest. Stop trying to please others… it’s IMPOSSIBLE to meet other people’s expectations. Listen, financial success, standing ovations and social recognition may bring temporary satisfaction to your life, but they can also become a trap. Own YOUR thoughts, own YOUR identity — own YOUR life! That is the #1 thing necessary to achieve success in life. #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: How can I sell my invention?
Answer: Luigi is seeking a $250,000 investment in exchange for 25% of his company. Luigi is a brilliant man, he owns multiple patents and inventions — however his inventions have not translated into profit. “Luigi, what’s your business strategy?” Mario asked. Luigi avoided Mario’s question focusing entirely on his product. “Luigi,” Mario insisted, “how do you plan to sell this furniture? Do you have a plan?” Luigi’s presentation had been enough to convince Mario that his innovation was great, yet he continued to show Mario the features of his prefabricated furniture. “Luigi, your product is great. I now need to understand how are you are going to make money with your invention.” Now, to answer your question, how can I sell my invention? Your invention is just a product, NOT yet a business. Success happens only when when have an innovative product with an effective business model around it. The best way to sell your invention, is to sell it not as an invention, but as a business. Your challenge? Having entrepreneurial skills is very different from having the ability to invent products or services. Perfect example: Steve Wozniak — The inventor Steve Jobs — The entrepreneur Each a genius in their own way. #BeBusinessSmart
